key_insight: Trauma-care conference respondents recognized LLMs’ potential efficiency benefits while emphasizing education, quality auditing, and oversight.
clinical_relevance: Integrating LLMs into trauma care and medical education requires attention to accuracy, patient safety, and preservation of clinical reasoning skills.
method: Descriptive analysis of pre- and post-conference surveys.
Clinical LLM use and attitudes assessed among 62 clinicians.
Rapid qualitative content analysis of 23 conference note-taking documents.
evidence_signal: Among 62 clinicians, 15% reported daily LLM use and 26% never used LLMs; among 52 post-conference respondents, 96% supported including LLM education in clinical curricula.
watch_item: These conference-based, self-reported findings describe attitudes and use, not demonstrated improvements in clinical outcomes or safety.
paper_title: Current Attitudes and Use Patterns of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice and Medical Education Among Trauma Providers
